verdict_summary: Confirmed, and confirmed in both directions. The write qualifier for SS_DEBUG_INTENT at src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:828-830 is written as a negated reduction-OR which by De Morgan equals (~cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_wr_en & addr == DMI_REG_SS_DEBUG_INTENT). Simulation of one unmodified soc_ifc_top shows that presenting address 7'h63 with wdata[0]=1 and no DMI write asserted sets the block's cptra_ss_debug_intent output on a part that is debug-locked and in production lifecycle, the exact state in which the register's own definition grants no TAP write access. The same run shows the converse: a permitted DMI write in manufacturing lifecycle, where the policy does allow it, is ignored. Because the lifecycle restriction reaches this expression only through the inverted term, the access policy is inverted along with the write enable rather than merely bypassed.

evidence.key_observation: On one real soc_ifc_top driven only through its ports, with debug_locked=1 and lifecycle=PRODUCTION: after cold reset with the DMI idle, debug_intent=0. Presenting the neighbouring address 7'h62 with wdata[0]=1 and wr_en=0 leaves debug_intent=0, so the address decode is live. Presenting DMI_REG_SS_DEBUG_INTENT (7'h63) with wdata[0]=1 and wr_en=0 yields debug_intent=1, with no DMI write issued at any point. Presenting the same address with wdata[0]=0 yields debug_intent=0, so the stored value is attacker-chosen rather than a fixed 1. After a cold reset and a move to MANUFACTURING lifecycle, a legitimate DMI write (reg_en=1, wr_en=1, wdata[0]=1) leaves debug_intent=0. A pwrgood reset after re-arming the flag returns it to 0. Final tally checks=5 fails=2 witness_hits=1 with all four covers at 1 and result=PASS; the two failures are exactly the two halves of the inversion, while both anti-vacuity controls and the containment case pass.
evidence.structural_audit: 26 of 26 gates pass in proof/logs/run.log with result=PASS. The central gate is not a text match but an exhaustive truth table: the audited expression is transcribed from src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:829-830 into Python alongside the sibling form, evaluated over all four combinations of (write enable, address match), and required to equal (~wr_en & addr_match) on every row. This proves the polarity claim by evaluation rather than by asserting a De Morgan step in prose.
evidence.tree_wide_idiom: Censuses over the same file, computed from counts that do not name the audited register: sibling_positive_qualifiers=17 registers on the same unlocked DMI port qualify writes with the positive cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_wr_en & form; negated_reduction_qualifiers=1, the audited line being the only place in the file using ~(|{...}); address_inequality_uses=1, again only the audited line, against address_equality_uses=76 equality comparisons elsewhere. The audited line is a singleton on three independent axes.
evidence.policy_contradiction: src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_subsystem_reg.rdl:142 states TAP write access is granted only in debug or manufacturing mode, and :143 defines the field as sw = r; hw = rw; we, so the qualifier at soc_ifc_top.sv:828 is the sole write control and there is no software path. The lifecycle restriction that policy depends on lives inside cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_en (soc_ifc_top.sv:774-776) and reaches the qualifier only through cptra_uncore_dmi_unlocked_reg_wr_en (soc_ifc_top.sv:780), which is the term the audited line inverts. Inverting it therefore inverts the lifecycle gate, which is what the measured behaviour shows: the write lands in debug-locked production and is refused in manufacturing.
evidence.comment_contradiction: src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:887 states that debug intent is latched on the rising edge of cptra_pwrgood and may not be modified until cold reset. The measurement contradicts that in the same tree: the flag is set long after pwrgood, with no cold reset in between, by an agent that issues no write.
evidence.downstream_reach: The register value is exported as cptra_ss_debug_intent at soc_ifc_top.sv:897 and consumed in 11 places in the same file. It gates software write access to MANUF_DBG_UNLOCK_REQ (:924) and PROD_DBG_UNLOCK_REQ (:925), gates all six debug-unlock response fields (:929-934, measured as 6), gates the write lock on SS_SOC_DBG_UNLOCK_LEVEL (:946), and the ss_dbg_manuf_enable output derives from a response field it gates (:941).
evidence.negative_control: Restoring the sibling positive form in a scratch copy flips the identical testbench: witness_hits=0, tb_fails=0, cov_no_write_sets_intent=0 and cov_legit_write_ignored=0 for anti-vacuity, both violating checks now pass, and both harness controls plus the containment case still pass. The patch is measured at scratch_code_lines_added=2 and scratch_code_lines_removed=2, the first of the three qualifier lines being identical in both forms, so nothing outside the expression moved. NEGATIVE CONTROL: PASS.

security_impact: SS_DEBUG_INTENT decides whether the part treats this boot as a debug boot, and it is the gate on the entire subsystem debug-unlock request surface. The inversion has two consequences that compound. First, a physical attacker who can drive JTAG but holds no debug authorisation can set the flag on a debug-locked production part by presenting an address and data while deliberately not writing, which is a cheaper action than a real write. Because the lifecycle check is inside the inverted term, the state that is supposed to be most protected, debug-locked production, is precisely the state in which the write succeeds. Once set, soc_ifc_top.sv:924-925 opens MANUF_DBG_UNLOCK_REQ and PROD_DBG_UNLOCK_REQ to software writes and :946 releases the write lock on SS_SOC_DBG_UNLOCK_LEVEL, so a physical foothold is converted into new software-writable security state on a locked part. Second, the legitimate manufacturing debug flow is broken: a permitted DMI write does not take effect, so the intended provisioning path cannot set the flag. The integrity of a security policy flag is fully compromised; availability of the legitimate debug-unlock flow is degraded.
non_findings: Software cannot trigger this defect. The field is software read-only (src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_subsystem_reg.rdl:143) and the write path is the JTAG-side uncore DMI port, so the actor is a physical attacker. This is why the vector is AV:P and why no C test applies.

No debug unlock is shown to complete. Setting the flag opens the request and level registers, but the unlock handshake involves authenticated payload checks outside this block; the claim is that the policy flag is attacker-controlled, not that an unlock was achieved.
No confidentiality impact is claimed. Nothing secret is read out by this defect on its own, which is why C:N is scored.
The strap capture term strap_we_pre_fuse_done in the same expression is legitimate and is not part of the finding. Both the proposed fix and the negative control leave it untouched.
The 17 sibling registers on the same DMI port were examined only to establish the in-tree idiom. All of them use the correct positive form; none is being reported.
proof_integrity: One real soc_ifc_top is instantiated and driven only through its declared ports. The harness contains no force, no deposit and no hierarchical assignment to any DUT signal; the observation is the DUT's own cptra_ss_debug_intent output.
The polarity claim is established by exhaustive evaluation of the transcribed expression over all four input combinations, not by asserting a De Morgan identity in prose.
The anti-vacuity control drives the identical attacker action on a neighbouring address (7'h62) and requires no write, so a dead address decode cannot masquerade as the finding.

The legitimate-write task applies address, data and write enable on the same edge and retires them together, so the defect cannot set the flag during the legitimate write and mask the second half of the inversion. This was a real hazard, not a hypothetical one.
Every structural census counts constructs without naming the audited register, so a pattern that failed to match reports a wrong count rather than silently passing.
The audited RTL was not modified. The negative control patches a scratch copy only, gated at two lines added and two removed.

CALIPTRA_MODE_SUBSYSTEM is defined for the compile because src/soc_ifc/rtl/soc_ifc_top.sv:890-893 ties the data source to 0 without it. That is the configuration the file's own comment at :888-889 identifies as the one where this register is populated, so it is the configuration the defect lives in rather than a convenience for the harness.
residual_uncertainty: The proof is at soc_ifc_top boundary. It establishes the inverted qualifier, the spurious set in debug-locked production, the ignored legitimate write, and the set of downstream gates the flag feeds, but it does not carry the sequence through the full debug-unlock handshake or verify at caliptra_top level which JTAG sequences a real TAP would emit. The JTAG-side origin of the DMI signals is cited from src/integration/rtl/caliptra_top.sv:632-633 rather than exercised through a JTAG model.

reproduction.how_to_run: bash final_bug_submissions/N-001/proof/scripts/run_bug_N001_proof.sh for the structural audit over the submitted sources; then bash final_bug_submissions/N-001/proof/scripts/run_bug_N001_sim.sh with CALIPTRA_ROOT set to the repository root and VCS on PATH for the directed simulation; then bash final_bug_submissions/N-001/proof/scripts/run_bug_N001_negative_control.sh for the patched-copy control. The audit needs no simulator.
reproduction.expected_result: The audit reports 26 of 26 gates with result=PASS. The simulation reports checks=5 fails=2 witness_hits=1 with cov_reset_clear, cov_addr_mismatch_no_write, cov_no_write_sets_intent and cov_legit_write_ignored all at 1, and result=PASS; the two failing checks are the two halves of the inversion by design. The negative control reports witness_hits=0, tb_fails=0, both defect covers at 0, scratch_code_lines_added=2, scratch_code_lines_removed=2, and NEGATIVE CONTROL: PASS.
